title: Apollo 13: 'Houston, we've had a problem' (control)
setting: Air-to-ground loop plus Mission Control flight-director loop, minutes after the oxygen tank explosion. Speaker labels are as printed in the Apollo Flight Journal. Journal commentary and photo captions interleaved in the web page are omitted (transcript lines only, in original order, one contiguous time range).
public_domain_basis: NASA mission transcript (US Government work). The Journal's editorial commentary is not used except as evidence quotes. Retrieved via a web.archive.org copy (https://web.archive.org/web/20240311202646id_/https://www.nasa.gov/history/afj/ap13fj/08day3-problem.html) because the live NASA URL now redirects to a generic page.

turns.speaker: Swigert
turns.text: Okay, Houston...

turns.speaker: Lovell
turns.text: ...Houston...

turns.speaker: Swigert
turns.text: ...we've had a problem here. [Pause.]

turns.speaker: Fenner (GUIDO)
turns.text: FLIGHT, GUIDANCE.

turns.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
turns.text: Go GUIDANCE.

turns.speaker: Lousma
turns.text: This is Houston. Say again, please.

turns.speaker: Fenner (GUIDO)
turns.text: We've had a Hardware Restart. I don't know what it was.

turns.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
turns.text: Okay. GNC, you want to take a look at it? See if you see any problems?

turns.speaker: Lovell
turns.text: [Garble.] Ah, Houston, we've had a problem. We've had a Main B Bus Undervolt.

turns.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
turns.text: Roger, we're copying it, CapCom. We see a hardware restart.

turns.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
turns.text: You see an AC Bus Undervolt there, GUIDANCE - ehhhm EECOM?

turns.speaker: Lousma
turns.text: Roger. Main B Undervolt. [Long pause.]

turns.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
turns.text: Negative, FLIGHT

turns.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
turns.text: I believe the crew reported it.

turns.speaker: Lousma (CAPCOM)
turns.text: We've got a Main Bus B undervolt.

turns.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
turns.text: Okay, flight, we've got some instrumentation funnies. Let me add them up.

turns.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
turns.text: Roger.

turns.speaker: Lousma
turns.text: Okay, stand by, 13. We're looking at it. [Pause.]

turns.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
turns.text: We may have had an instrumentation problem, FLIGHT.

turns.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
turns.text: Rog.

turns.speaker: Glines (INCO)
turns.text: FLIGHT, INCO.

turns.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
turns.text: Go, INCO.

turns.speaker: Glines (INCO)
turns.text: We switched to wide beam width about the time he had that problem.

turns.speaker: Haise
turns.text: Okay. Right now, Houston, the voltage is - is looking good. And we had a pretty large bang associated with the Caution and Warning there. And as I recall, Main B was the one that had had an amp spike on it once before. [Pause.]

turns.speaker: Lousma
turns.text: Roger, Fred. [Long pause.]

documented_events.what_happened: Lovell's report of the anomaly; the actual wording was 'Houston, we've had a problem', a calm cooperative report, not the film's 'we have a problem'.
documented_events.evidence_quote: The legendary line delivered by Lovell is "Houston, we've had a problem" and not the familiar "Houston, we have a problem" made especially popular by the Tom Hanks movie. The writers of the movie have admitted that they had to use the line expected by the viewers, instead of the historically accurate one, for the sake of drama. This of course has perpetuated the line in the popular consciousness, putting it into the top three of misquoted movies

documented_events.what_happened: Crew and controllers initially treat the event as a probable instrumentation false alarm while the crew report a real bang.
documented_events.evidence_quote: Although both the crew and the mission controllers are suspecting that this is a false alarm generated by spurious sensor readings, the bang is a genuine worry.

notes: Real urgency, terse cooperation, no manipulation. Both documented events are commentary from the Apollo Flight Journal (NASA-hosted, contributor-written), not an official investigation; the Apollo 13 Review Board report was not fetched. Timestamps stripped from turns. Overlap in first two turns is in the source.
